name: groupadd
description: Creates a new group. Groups collect users to simplify permission management.

flags.description: Create a system group with a GID below 1000.
Exit successfully if the group already exists.

examples.explanation: Adds alice to the new group (groups only become useful once users join).
Assigns a directory tree to the group so every member shares access.
Shows the group entry and its members.

about: Groups are stored in /etc/group. A user has one primary group (in /etc/passwd) and any number of supplementary groups. New files created by a user inherit their primary group unless the directory has the SGID bit set, which forces inheritance of the directory's group — the key trick for shared folders.
mistakes: Creating a group but forgetting to add users or set directory group ownership.
Expecting group changes to apply to running sessions — users must re-login.
